questions.text:
An instruction format has the following structure:

Instruction Number: [latex]Opcode \; \; destination reg, \;\; source reg-1, \;\;source reg-2[/latex]

Consider the following sequence of instructions to be executed in a pipelined processor:

I1: DIV R3, R1, R2
I2: SUB R5, R3, R4
I3: ADD R3, R5, R6
I4: MUL R7, R3, R8

Which of the following statements is/are TRUE
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I1 writes R3, I2 reads R3 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] RAW [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- I1 and I3 both write R3 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] that is WAW, not WAR [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- I2 reads R3, I3 writes R3 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] that is WAR, not RAW [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- I3 writes R3, I4 reads R3 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] that is RAW, not WAW [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.

Answer: There is a RAW dependency on R3 between I1 and I2

options: There is a RAW dependency on R3 between I1 and I2
There is a WAR dependency on R3 between I1 and I3
There is a RAW dependency on R3 between I2 and I3
There is a WAW dependency on R3 between I3 and I4

questions.text: Which of the following fields of an IP header is/are always modified by any router before it forwards the IP packet?
questions.solution:
Every router decrements the TTL. Since a header field changed, the header checksum must be recomputed too.

Source IP and protocol are not changed by an ordinary router (source IP changes only with NAT, which is not "any router").

Answer: TTL, Header Checksum

fX moves pointer [latex]b[/latex] until it reaches '\0' and returns [latex]b-a[/latex], i.e. the string length.

- fX("abcd"): string literal is null terminated [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] returns 4.
- char c[] = "abcd": array of 5 chars including '\0' [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] returns 4.
- char *c = "abcd": points to a null-terminated literal [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] returns 4.
- The code is valid C (pointer difference converted to int) [latex]\text{---}[/latex] it compiles.

Answer: Options 1, 2 and 4

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: The function call fX("abcd") will always return a value
Assuming a character array c is declared as char c[] = "abcd" in main(), the function call fX(c)will always return a value
The code of the function will not compile
Assuming a character pointer c is declared as char *c = "abcd" in main(), the function call fX(c)will always return a value

questions.text:
Let [latex] P [/latex] be the partial order defined on the set [latex] \{1,2,3,4\} [/latex] as follows
[latex] P=\{(x, x) \mid x \in\{1,2,3,4\}\} \cup\{(1,2),(3,2),(3,4)\} [/latex]
The number of total orders on [latex] \{1,2,3,4\} [/latex] that contain [latex] P [/latex] is ______
questions.solution:
A total order containing P must keep [latex]1 \lt 2,\ 3 \lt 2,\ 3 \lt 4[/latex]. Count such orderings (linear extensions).

The first element must be 1 or 3 (nothing must come before them).
- Start with 1: next must be 3 (both 2 and 4 need 3 first), then 2, 4 in any order [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 1324, 1342 (2 orders).
- Start with 3: arrange 1, 2, 4 with 1 before 2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 3124, 3142, 3412 (3 orders).

Total = 5

Answer: 5

questions.text: Let [latex] A [/latex] be an array containing integer values. The distance of [latex] A [/latex] is defined as the minimum number of elements in [latex] A [/latex] that must be replaced with another integer so that the resulting array is sorted in non-decreasing order. The distance of the array [latex] [2,5,3,1,4,2,6] [/latex] is _____
questions.solution:
Elements we keep must already be in non-decreasing order; all others can be replaced by suitable values. So
distance = [latex]n-[/latex] (length of longest non-decreasing subsequence).

In [2, 5, 3, 1, 4, 2, 6] the longest non-decreasing subsequence is 2, 3, 4, 6 (length 4).

Distance [latex]=7-4=3[/latex] (e.g. [2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 6]).

Answer: 3
